text:
michael: Heads-up — CI microbench 'batcher_harvest' failed on PR #5280. Threshold diff +12.3% p50, failing the perf gate. /cc @anna @raj
ci-bot: [perf-run] PR:5280 — batcher_harvest | baseline=12.34ms new=13.86ms delta=+12.29% (threshold=+5.00%) — full logs: https://ci.redwood/invocations/abcd1234
anna: Yikes. Is there a short repro we can run locally?
raj: Run this locally: `tools/perf/run_microbench --bench batcher_harvest --runs 200 --seed 42` — I repro'd ~+11% on my T4.
lisa: Any notable changes in the PR? It was mainly the scheduler refactor and a small tweak to KV eviction ordering.
raj: Yep — PR 5279/5280 introduced a micro-optim to batch wait heuristics (move to max-wait fallback) and flipped an eviction priority flag. I suspected it might affect packing.
michael: CI flamegraph attached in the logs shows more time in scheduler::select_batches and recv path. snippet: ```
# flamegraph top
scheduler::select_batches  36%
kv::get  8%
compute::attention  40%
```
anna: Hmm scheduler time up 36% vs baseline? That aligns with p50 shift. Can we bisect to the exact commit?
raj: I'm running git-bisect locally between commit aa1f8 (pre) and 8c3e4b (post). Early results point at commit 8c3e4b (the 'dynamic-wait' change).
ci-bot: bisect job started by raj — https://ci.redwood/bisect/9876 — will post results when done
michael: If it's the dynamic-wait change, maybe the new heuristic increases head-of-line latency for many small requests because batches wait longer to fill. Could explain increased p50.
lisa: Also worth noting that KV miss rate in the CI traces increased from 2.1% -> 3.7% after the merge. That could amplify scheduler pressure (more KV fetch stalls).
anna: Agreed. Plan: (1) raj finish bisect; (2) I will run a dedicated infra run with KV disabled to isolate; (3) if bisect confirms, we either revert or hotfix to the previous wait policy.
raj: Bisect finished: culprit=commit 8c3e4b (dynamic-wait: use target_batch_util instead of min_wait_ms). Repro is consistent.
michael: Thanks. Can we try a quick toggle to restore old behavior (config flag) and rerun microbench in CI as a patch? If that fixes, mark as rollback and un-block release.
raj: I'll open PR to add `--use-legacy-wait` flag and run the microbench job. Draft: #5291.
lisa: Marking this as rollout blocker for the next deploy. :lock: Please don't merge new runtime changes until resolved.
ci-bot: Triggered perf job for PR #5291 — awaiting results.
devops-bot: FYI ops: hold the v1.3.2 rollout window until perf gate clears. Notifying release leads.
michael: If the flag reverts perf to baseline, we should cherry-pick the fix to the release branch and then iterate on a less aggressive heuristic.
anna: I'll run dedicated infra runs (longer sampling) and check KV miss correlation. ETA 2hrs.
raj: PR #5291 shows microbench delta: baseline=12.36ms new=12.40ms delta=+0.3% — within threshold. Will propose cherry-pick to release.
lisa: Nice. After cherry-pick let's re-run full perf suite and confirm KV miss is stable.
michael: Excellent. Thanks team. Leave the bisect logs and flamegraphs linked in the PR. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: All CI artifacts copied to PR #5291: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/5291/perf
anna: I'll post a short postmortem after we confirm and revert the rollout hold.
raj: Added a small note in PR description about follow-up: tune target_batch_util to avoid increased head-of-line latency.
michael: Cool — once cherry-pick goes out, we can close this thread.
